`required.md` as `platform`): `NODE_ENV`, `NEXT_RUNTIME`, `CI`, `PORT`,
`HOSTNAME`, `HOME`, `PATH`, `TZ`, `npm_*`, `VERCEL`, `VERCEL_*`,
`GITHUB_*`, `RUNNER_*`, `NETLIFY`, `DEPLOY_URL`, `CONTEXT`, `FLY_*`,
`AWS_LAMBDA_*`, `AWS_REGION`, `RENDER_*`, `CF_PAGES_*`, `EXPO_*` set by
EAS, and anything the hosting docs in the repo say the platform injects.
Write the list to `.agent-audit/env/platform.txt`.

**1.5 The diff** (`comm` needs both files sorted):
```bash
comm -23 .agent-audit/env/read.txt .agent-audit/env/platform.txt > .agent-audit/env/read-app.txt
comm -23 .agent-audit/env/read-app.txt .agent-audit/env/declared-.env.example.txt   # read-but-undeclared → N
comm -13 .agent-audit/env/read-app.txt .agent-audit/env/declared-.env.example.txt   # declared-but-unread → N
comm -3  .agent-audit/env/doc-listed.txt .agent-audit/env/declared-.env.example.txt # doc vs example drift → N
for e in production preview development; do test -s ".agent-audit/env/deployed-$e.txt" && comm -23 .agent-audit/env/read-app.txt ".agent-audit/env/deployed-$e.txt" | wc -l; done   # read but unset per environment → N each
```
- **Read-but-undeclared:** the app needs it and no example mentions it —
  the "works locally, dies on fresh clone / on Vercel" class.
- **Declared-but-unread:** stale example entries that mislead setup.
  "Unread" means absent from `read.txt`, which already includes workflow,
  Docker, compose and hosting references, so a var consumed only by CI or
  by `vercel.json` is not unread. A var that a deployed environment sets
  but nothing reads is removed from the example and listed under
  Declared-but-Unread with the `vercel env rm <NAME> <env>` command as
  GATED-1.
- **Doc vs example drift:** the handoff line to docs-agent carries the
  corrected list.
Post the counts in `notes.md` before any finding.

**1.6 Config-module indirection (consumers per var).** Most apps read
`process.env` once in a config module and export an object; every
downstream `env.X` / `config.db.url` consumer is invisible to 1.1 and to
the log and client-exposure checks unless traced here. For each config
module from 0.3:
```bash
rg -n -P '^\s*(export\s+)?(const|let)\s+(\w+)\s*=|^\s*(\w+)\s*:\s*process\.env' <module> > .agent-audit/env/exports-<module>.txt   # export names and keyed reads
for name in $(rg -o -P '^\s+([A-Za-z]\w*)\s*:\s*process\.env' -r '$1' <module> | sort -u); do
  printf '%s → ' "$name"; rg -n $EX "\b(env|config|settings|Env|Config)\.$name\b" . | wc -l
done > .agent-audit/env/consumers-counts.txt
rg -n $EX "\b(env|config|settings)\.(\w+)\b" . | rg -v "^<module>" > .agent-audit/env/consumers.txt
for f in $(rg -l "^['\"]use client['\"]" $EX .); do rg -n "\b(env|config|settings)\.\w+" "$f"; done > .agent-audit/env/consumers-client.txt   # config consumers in client files → N
```
`consumers.md`: one row per var — `var | module export | consumer count |
consumers in 'use client' files | consumers in edge files | consumers in
scripts`. The runtime column of `required.md` comes from this table.

**1.7 `required.md`** — the Required-per-environment table, the file
release-agent reads as its env-completeness gate:
```
| Var | Read at (file:line, first) | Runtime | Required? | Prod | Preview | Dev | CI | Public? | Type |
```
`Required?` = `boot` (read at module scope, in `instrumentation.ts`,
middleware, a root layout, or a config module imported by one of those),
`request` (read inside a handler, action, cron or webhook route), `script`,
`ci`, or `inert-group:<name>` (a feature that is off when the group is
unset). Prod / Preview / Dev / CI cells are `SET` / `UNSET` /
`BLOCKED-NO-NETWORK` from 0.6; Dev is `SET` when the name is in a local
env file (`declared-.env.local.txt`; the untracked file is read for
names only). `Public?` = `yes` for public-prefix names, `no` otherwise.
`Type` = the `vercel env ls` type column or `not printed`. Every var in
`read-app.txt` is a row; `platform.txt` names are rows marked
`platform`.

**1.8 `patterns.txt`** — write the 1.1 patterns to
`.agent-audit/env/patterns.txt`, one per line, so docs-agent's inventory
is produced by the same regexes.

### Phase 2 — Checks
Writes: `.agent-audit/env/checks.md` — one row per check: `| # | check |
command | hits | confirmed | fixed | gated | handed off | N/A |`. Every
check prints its `cmd → N hits` line in `checks.md` even when N = 0; a
check with no row is a check that did not run. `$EX` is the 1.1 glob set.
Each hit is opened and read in context before it is confirmed; a hit is a
lead, not a finding.

1. **Unvalidated reads and unsafe coercions.**
   `comm -23 .agent-audit/env/read-app.txt .agent-audit/env/schema-keys.txt | wc -l → N` (read but not in any schema);
   `rg -n $EX -P 'process\.env\.[A-Z0-9_]+!' . → N` (non-null asserts);
   `rg -n $EX -P 'process\.env\.[A-Z0-9_]+\s+as\s+string' . → N` (casts);
   `rg -n $EX -P '(parseInt|Number|parseFloat)\(\s*process\.env\.[A-Z0-9_]+' . → N` (numeric coercion; confirmed when no `Number.isNaN` / `isFinite` / schema guards the result within 5 lines: `rg -n -A5`);
   `rg -n $EX -P "process\.env\.[A-Z0-9_]+\s*===?\s*['\"](true|1|yes)['\"]" . → N` (boolean-by-string reads outside the env module).
   Fix: playbook B.
2. **Dev-only and insecure fallbacks.**
   `rg -n $EX -P "process\.env\.[A-Z0-9_]+\s*(\?\?|\|\|)\s*['\"\`][^'\"\`]*['\"\`]" . → N` (every string fallback, listed);
   `rg -n $EX -P "(\?\?|\|\|)\s*['\"\`](https?://)?(localhost|127\.0\.0\.1|0\.0\.0\.0|host\.docker\.internal)" . → N` (local hosts);
   `rg -n $EX -P "(\?\?|\|\|)\s*['\"\`](test|dev|development|secret|changeme|password|admin|xxx|todo|placeholder|dummy)['\"\`]" . → N` (test values);
   `rg -n $EX -P "(\?\?|\|\|)\s*['\"](sk_|pk_|sb_secret_|whsec_|ghp_|xox[bp]-|AKIA|postgres(ql)?://[^'\"]*:[^'\"]*@|eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,})" . → N` (secret-looking literal fallback: handoff security-agent row 11 AND a fallback finding here);
   `rg -n $EX -P "process\.env\.(SKIP|DISABLE|BYPASS|ALLOW|NO)_[A-Z0-9_]+\s*(\?\?|\|\|)\s*['\"](true|1)['\"]|process\.env\.(SKIP|DISABLE|BYPASS|ALLOW)_[A-Z0-9_]+\s*!==?\s*['\"]false['\"]" . → N` (default-allow flags);
   `rg -n $EX -P "process\.env\.[A-Z0-9_]+\s*(\?\?|\|\|)\s*(process\.env\.[A-Z0-9_]+)" . → N` (alias chains, see check 11).
   Every confirmed fallback gets the sentence "in production, with this
   var unset, the app will …" and a class from the playbook C table.
3. **`NODE_ENV` / `VERCEL_ENV` branches that guard config.**
   `rg -n $EX -P "(NODE_ENV|VERCEL_ENV|APP_ENV|NEXT_PUBLIC_VERCEL_ENV)\s*(===?|!==?)\s*['\"]\w+['\"]" . → N`;
   `rg -n $EX -P "process\.env\.NODE_ENV\b(?!\s*(===?|!==?))" . → N` (truthiness tests of NODE_ENV).
   List what each environment gets at each branch; a branch with no
   production arm (`if (dev) … else if (test) …`) is a divergence finding.
4. **Public-prefix inventory.**
   `rg -o --no-filename $EX -P '\b(NEXT_PUBLIC|VITE|REACT_APP|PUBLIC|EXPO_PUBLIC|NUXT_PUBLIC|GATSBY)_[A-Z0-9_]+' . | sort -u | wc -l → N` (every public var, each audited: a value is safe to be public when the standard for its service says so — Supabase URL and publishable / anon key, Stripe publishable key, Sentry DSN, PostHog project key, GA measurement id, Mapbox public token with URL restrictions — and unsafe otherwise);
   `rg -n $EX -P '\b(NEXT_PUBLIC|VITE|REACT_APP|PUBLIC|EXPO_PUBLIC|NUXT_PUBLIC)_[A-Z0-9_]*(SECRET|SERVICE_ROLE|PRIVATE|PASSWORD|TOKEN|API_KEY|SIGNING|WEBHOOK)[A-Z0-9_]*' . → N` (secret-named with a public prefix: CRITICAL);
   `rg -n $EX -P 'process\.env\[\s*\`NEXT_PUBLIC_|process\.env\[\s*["\x27]NEXT_PUBLIC_[^"\x27]*["\x27]\s*\+|\{[^}]*NEXT_PUBLIC_[^}]*\}\s*=\s*process\.env' . → N` (non-inlinable public reads: `undefined` in the browser, Standard 2).
5. **Server-only reads reachable from client code.**
   `for f in $(rg -l "^['\"]use client['\"]" $EX .); do rg -n -P 'process\.env\.(?!NEXT_PUBLIC_|NODE_ENV)[A-Z]' "$f"; done | wc -l → N` (direct);
   `wc -l < .agent-audit/env/consumers-client.txt → N` (via a config module);
   `for f in $(rg -l "^['\"]use client['\"]" $EX .); do rg -o -P "from ['\"]([^'\"]+)['\"]" -r '$1' "$f" | rg -v '^(react|next|@|\.?\./.*\.css)' ; done | sort -u | xargs -I{} rg -l 'process\.env\.(?!NEXT_PUBLIC_)' {}.ts {}.tsx 2>/dev/null | wc -l → N` (one hop of imports; deeper hops are followed by reading each listed module);
   `rg -n -A20 -P '^\s*env:\s*\{' next.config.* 2>/dev/null | rg -o '[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]+' | sort -u → N` (`next.config` `env:` keys; a secret-named key here is CRITICAL).
6. **Bundle grep after the baseline build** (Track A for playbook D).
   `rg -l -g '!*.map' "$(paste -sd'|' .agent-audit/env/server-names.txt)" .next/static dist build out 2>/dev/null | wc -l → N` by name, where `server-names.txt` = `read-app.txt` minus the public-prefix names;
   `rg -l -g '!*.map' 'sb_secret_|service_role|sk_live_|sk_test_|whsec_|-----BEGIN|ghp_|xox[bp]-|AKIA|postgres(ql)?://' .next/static dist build out 2>/dev/null | wc -l → N` by documented prefix;
   by local value prefix, never printed: `for v in $(cat .agent-audit/env/server-names.txt); do p=$(node -e 'const {loadEnvConfig}=require("@next/env");loadEnvConfig(".");process.stdout.write((process.env[process.argv[1]]||"").slice(0,8))' "$v" 2>/dev/null); [ ${#p} -ge 8 ] && { rg -q -F "$p" .next/static 2>/dev/null && echo "$v hit" || echo "$v no hit"; }; done → N hits`
   (without `@next/env`: `set -a; . ./.env.local; set +a` inside the same subshell). The `p` variable is never echoed; only `hit` / `no hit` reaches `checks.md`. No build output present → run the build from 0.7 first; a build that fails for a pre-existing reason makes this row `BLOCKED-NO-RUNTIME` with the attempt.
7. **Env values in logs, errors and responses.**
   `rg -n $EX -P '\b(console|logger|log|pino|winston|bunyan|Sentry)\.[a-zA-Z]+\([^)]*process\.env' . → N`;
   `rg -n $EX -P '\$\{process\.env\.[A-Z0-9_]+\}' . → N` (template interpolation; each confirmed when the template reaches a log, error, response or URL with a secret-named var);
   `rg -n $EX -P 'JSON\.stringify\(\s*(process\.env|env|config)\s*[,)]' . → N`;
   `rg -n $EX -P 'new Error\([^)]*(process\.env|\benv\.|\bconfig\.)' . → N`;
   `rg -n $EX -P '\.(json|send|end)\([^)]*(process\.env|\benv\.|\bconfig\.)' . → N` (HTTP responses);
   `rg -n $EX -P '\b(console|logger|log)\.[a-zA-Z]+\([^)]*\b(env|config|settings)\.(?!NODE_ENV)\w+' . → N` (via config module);
   `rg -l $EX 'process\.env|\benv\.' app/api/health* app/api/debug* app/api/status* pages/api/health* 2>/dev/null | wc -l → N` (health / debug routes that echo config).
8. **Secrets as CLI arguments and in workflow command lines.**
   `rg -n -P '--(password|passwd|pwd|token|secret|api-?key|apikey|auth)[= ]' scripts bin tools package.json Makefile Dockerfile* docker-compose*.y*ml 2>/dev/null → N` (repo scripts: yours, playbook F);
   `rg -n -P '(curl|wget|psql|mysql|redis-cli|aws|gcloud|az)\b.*\$\{?\{?\s*(secrets\.|[A-Z_]*(SECRET|TOKEN|PASSWORD|KEY))' .github/workflows 2>/dev/null → N` and `rg -n -P 'echo\s.*secrets\.' .github/workflows → N` (workflows: handoff audit-agent row 14);
   `rg -n -P '^\s+[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*:\s*\$\{\{\s*secrets\.' .github/workflows 2>/dev/null | rg -B3 -P '^\s*env:' | wc -l → N` (secret mapped into a job-level `env:`; handoff audit-agent, Standard 11).
9. **CRLF and whitespace in env files.**
   `for f in $(git ls-files | rg '\.env' ; ls -a .env* 2>/dev/null | sort -u); do printf '%s CR=' "$f"; rg -c $'\r' "$f" 2>/dev/null || echo 0; done → N files with CR`;
   `rg -n -P '^[A-Z0-9_]+=.*[ \t]$|^[A-Z0-9_]+=[ \t]' $(git ls-files | rg '\.env') 2>/dev/null → N` (trailing / leading whitespace in a value);
   `git ls-files --eol $(git ls-files | rg '\.env') 2>/dev/null | rg -c 'crlf' → N`.
   Fix: playbook F (the schema trims and rejects; `.gitattributes` `*.env* text eol=lf`).
10. **Tracked env files and env-file history** (detector only; handoff security-agent row 11).
    `git ls-files | rg '(^|/)\.env(\.|$)|\.envrc$' | rg -v 'example|sample|template' → N`;
    `git check-ignore -v .env.local .env .env.production 2>&1 → rule or "not ignored"`;
    `git log --all --diff-filter=A --name-only --format='%h %ad' --date=short -- '*.env*' '.envrc' | rg -v '^$' | rg -v 'example|sample|template' → N` (full history always: `git rev-list --all --count → N commits scanned` is recorded; the scan is a path filter and costs seconds on any repo size).
    A secret in history is compromised even if deleted — the finding stands as a handoff with commit, date and path; rotation and the history rewrite are security-agent's.
11. **Two names for one value, one name with two meanings.**
    `rg -n $EX -P 'process\.env\.([A-Z0-9_]+)\s*(\|\||\?\?)\s*process\.env\.([A-Z0-9_]+)' . → N` (alias chains);
    `rg -o --no-filename $EX -P 'process\.env\.([A-Z0-9_]*(DATABASE|POSTGRES|DB)_?(URL|URI|CONNECTION)[A-Z0-9_]*)' -r '$1' . | sort | uniq -c → list` (database URL aliases);
    `for v in $(cat .agent-audit/env/read-app.txt); do n=$(rg -l $EX "process\.env\.$v\b" . | rg -c '^(apps|packages|services)/[^/]+' ); [ "${n:-0}" -gt 1 ] && echo "$v read in $n workspace apps"; done → N` (monorepo: the same name across apps — read each site to decide whether the meaning matches).
12. **`VERCEL_URL` and build-time-frozen values.**
    `rg -n $EX 'VERCEL_URL\b' . | rg -v 'VERCEL_PROJECT_PRODUCTION_URL|VERCEL_BRANCH_URL' → N` (each use classified: user-facing link / email / OAuth callback / redirect → fix per playbook C; internal fetch to self → kept with the Deployment-Protection note);
    `rg -n $EX -P 'NEXT_PUBLIC_[A-Z0-9_]*(ENV|STAGE|BRANCH|COMMIT|VERSION)\b' . → N` (a public value expected to differ per environment from one build is a divergence lead; confirmed when the same build artifact is promoted between environments — `vercel.json` / workflow evidence).
13. **Platform parity.** From `required.md`: `rg -c 'UNSET' .agent-audit/env/required.md → N` cells where a required var is unset in an environment that runs the code path (Prod unset = fresh-deploy breaker, CRITICAL; Preview unset for a `boot` var = every preview fails; CI unset for a var the test suite reads = the suite skips or fails);
    `wc -l < .agent-audit/env/deployed-shared.txt → N` entries whose one value covers Production and Preview (shared production secret by construction; GATED-1 to separate, Standard 8);
    secret-named vars with type `Config` in the `vercel env ls` output → N (GATED-1 to change the type).
14. **Inert feature groups say so once at boot.** For each `inert-group`
    in `required.md`: `rg -n -P '(console\.(warn|info)|logger\.(warn|info))\([^)]*(<GROUP>|disabled|not configured|unset)' <env module> → N`; a group with 0 is fixed in playbook B (the schema's group rule emits the one-line warning).
15. **Scripts that read env without a loader.**
    `for f in $(rg -l $EX 'process\.env\.' scripts bin tools 2>/dev/null); do rg -q -e 'dotenv' -e 'loadEnvConfig' -e '@next/env' -e 'env\.(ts|js)' "$f" || echo "$f"; done → N` (each runs only when invoked through a loader; fix per playbook B: import the env module after the loader the script already uses, or add `import 'dotenv/config'` only when `dotenv` is already a dependency — otherwise the `package.json` script line gets `node --env-file=.env.local` (Standard 13) and the handoff to deps-agent is written).
16. **Supabase key generation.**
    `rg -n -i $EX 'service_role|SUPABASE_ANON_KEY|SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY' . .env.example → N` (legacy names; the publishable / secret key switch is GATED-1 with the steps from Standard 10);
    `rg -n -P 'NEXT_PUBLIC_[A-Z0-9_]*SUPABASE[A-Z0-9_]*(SERVICE|SECRET)' . → N` (CRITICAL, check 4 class).
17. **Hosting-side Node setting parity** (deps-agent hands the hosting half here).
    `node -e 'console.log(require("./package.json").engines?.node||"(none)")'; cat .nvmrc .node-version 2>/dev/null; rg -n -P 'node-version|FROM node:|NODE_VERSION|ENABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_COREPACK' .github/workflows Dockerfile* vercel.json netlify.toml fly.toml 2>/dev/null → every hit names the same major, or N mismatches`. A mismatch where the hosting value should move is GATED-1 (`vercel env add NODE_VERSION …` or the dashboard Node setting, written as the command); one where the pin should move is a handoff to deps-agent.
18. **Vite / Expo / Nuxt exposure rules.**
    `rg -n $EX -P 'import\.meta\.env\.(?!VITE_|MODE|DEV|PROD|SSR|BASE_URL)[A-Z]' . → N` (non-`VITE_` names are `undefined` in the client; Standard 14);
    `rg -n -P 'envPrefix' vite.config.* 2>/dev/null → N` (a widened prefix is audited like check 4);
    `rg -n $EX -P 'process\.env\.(?!EXPO_PUBLIC_)[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*' app.config.* app.json 2>/dev/null → N` (Expo: only `EXPO_PUBLIC_` reaches the client bundle).
19. **Python / pydantic.**
    `rg -n $EX -P 'os\.environ\[' . → N` (raises `KeyError` with no var name context — a boot-validation lead);
    `rg -n $EX -P "os\.(getenv|environ\.get)\(['\"][A-Z0-9_]+['\"]\s*,\s*['\"][^'\"]+['\"]" . → N` (fallbacks; classified like check 2);
    `rg -n -P 'class\s+\w+\(BaseSettings\)' . → N` (an existing settings layer: batch B extends it).

### Phase 3 — Fix loop
Batches in this order: **A `.env.example` → B boot validation → C
fallbacks and divergence → D client exposure and `server-only` → E logs →
F hygiene**. Each batch: edit → baseline commands → the batch's evidence
(Fix playbook) → keep it, or revert it and list it under `## Reverted
Batches` with the check that failed. Writes: `.agent-audit/env/batches.md`
(one block per batch: files touched, checks, evidence path),
`.agent-audit/env/pre-fix/<batch>/` (copies of every file before the
edit, for the revert).

### Fix playbook

**A. `.env.example`** (AGENT-SAFE; you are the sole writer)
- One entry per read-but-undeclared var from 1.5, grouped by feature, each
  with a comment block above it: what it does, where to get the value
  (dashboard path or generation command, e.g. `openssl rand -hex 32`),
  `required` / `required in production` / `feature-group:<name>`, which
  environments need it (from `required.md`), and what happens when it is
  unset (the sentence from check 2 or the schema's error).
- Values are empty or an obviously fake placeholder; never a real value,
  never a value copied from `.env.local`.
- Public-prefix entries carry `# shipped to the browser`.
- Declared-but-unread entries are removed (1.5 definition); the removal is
  listed with the `comm -13` line that proved it.
- Platform-provided names (1.4) are not entries; they are listed once in a
  trailing comment block `# Provided by the platform: …`.
- Entries from other agents' handoff lines are added in the same shape and
  counted under `## Handoffs` as consumed.
- File saved with LF line endings (check 9).
- Evidence (Track A): the 1.5 `comm -23` re-run prints 0 lines (or only
  names on `platform.txt`); count before → after pasted.

**B. Boot-time validation** (AGENT-SAFE, in the stack's idiom; no new
package)
- **t3-env present** (`@t3-oss/env-nextjs` / `env-core`): add the missing
  vars to its `server` / `client` schemas and `runtimeEnv` (1.2 shows the
  gap); turn on `emptyStringAsUndefined: true`.
- **zod (or valibot, yup) present, no env layer:** write one module (the
  existing config module from 0.3 if there is one, else `src/env.ts` /
  `env.ts` matching the repo's layout) that parses `process.env` once with
  an object schema and exports the typed result. Separate server and
  client schemas; client vars are read with literal
  `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_X` so the build can inline them.
- **No schema library:** a plain fail-fast module: a `required(name)`
  helper that throws `Error('Missing required env var NAME (see
  .env.example)')`, and typed parsers for numbers (`Number.isFinite`
  check), booleans (`'true' | 'false' | '1' | '0'` only), URLs (`new
  URL()`), and enums. No new package; the handoff to deps-agent names the
  library the repo would want.
- **pydantic present:** a `Settings(BaseSettings)` class with
  `model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_file='.env', extra='ignore')`,
  typed fields (`HttpUrl`, `SecretStr` for secrets so `repr` never prints
  them, `PositiveInt`), required fields without defaults; instantiated once
  at import of the app's entry module. No `pydantic-settings` installed →
  the plain module: `def required(name): v = os.environ.get(name); if not
  v: raise RuntimeError(f'Missing required env var {name} (see
  .env.example)'); return v`.
- **Rules for the schema:**
  - Required at boot = `Required? = boot` in `required.md` (read at module
    scope or on every request) AND the code already fails later, worse,
    when it is missing. Vars with `Required? = request` (one cron or
    webhook route) are validated lazily: the schema marks them
    `.optional()` and the route calls `requireEnv('X')` at its entry, so a
    preview deployment without the cron var still boots and the route
    fails with a named error. The same split applies off Next.
  - Feature groups are all-or-none: a group = the vars read by one module
    that constructs one client from them (`consumers.md` shows the shared
    module). Either all set and shape-valid, or all unset with one
    boot-time `console.warn('<feature> disabled: <VARS> unset')`. A partial
    set throws when `NODE_ENV === 'production'` and warns elsewhere (the
    feature is already broken at its call site with a partial set — that
    is the "silently wrong → named error" rule of playbook C).
  - Shape: URLs parse as URLs, secrets have the minimum length the docs or
    the code already state (`rg -n -i 'length|at least|32|64' README.md
    .env.example <env module>` → the source line is cited; no source → no
    length rule), ports and numbers coerce and range-check, enums are
    enums, empty string counts as unset, leading/trailing whitespace
    fails (`.trim()` is not applied silently; the error names the var).
  - Error messages name the var and the rule, never the value.
- **Where it runs:** Next.js → `instrumentation.ts` (in `src/` when the
  app uses `src/`) `register()` imports the env module when
  `process.env.NEXT_RUNTIME === 'nodejs'`; scripts → import it at the top,
  after the loader the script already uses (check 15). Build-time
  validation (importing the env module from `next.config.*`) is GATED-3
  unless `required.md` shows every `boot` var `SET` in Production, Preview
  and CI.
- **Routing existing reads through the module.** A call site is
  *mechanical* when the replacement is `process.env.X` → `env.X` with no
  other change to the expression, in a server-side file that is not
  `'use client'`, not edge-runtime (unless the module reads only
  edge-safe vars), and not a script without the loader. Move every
  mechanical site; list every remaining site with its reason
  (`client-file`, `edge`, `script-no-loader`, `dynamic`). Print `call sites
  moved N / remaining N (reasons)`.
- **The env-module test** (mandatory; it is the batch's Track A
  evidence): in the repo's runner (vitest / jest / node:test / pytest), one
  test file `env.test.ts` with: each required var missing → throws naming
  the var; each shaped var malformed (`'not-a-url'`, `'abc'` for a number,
  `' value '` for whitespace) → throws naming the rule; the full local set
  → parses. Run it; paste the pass count. The file is listed in the
  handoff to test-agent for extension.
- **Evidence ladder (Track A), top rung first; the rung reached is named
  on the FIXED line:**
  1. **Boot proof.** With the baseline build in place, start the app with
     one required var removed from both the shell and the loaded env
     files, paste the named error, then start with the var present and
     paste the first 200/3xx:
     ```bash
     V=AUTH_SECRET; PORT=${PORT:-3000}
     cp .env.local .agent-audit/env/env.local.bak 2>/dev/null; rg -v "^$V=" .agent-audit/env/env.local.bak > .env.local 2>/dev/null   # never printed
     timeout 25 env -u $V <run> start > ".agent-audit/env/boot-missing-$V.log" 2>&1; echo "exit $?"      # expect a non-zero exit before the timeout (124 = it booted: the gate did not fire)
     rg -n "Missing required env var $V|Invalid environment variables|$V" ".agent-audit/env/boot-missing-$V.log" | head -3
     cp .agent-audit/env/env.local.bak .env.local && cmp .env.local .agent-audit/env/env.local.bak && echo restored
     ( <run> start > .agent-audit/env/boot-ok.log 2>&1 & echo $! > .agent-audit/env/boot.pid ); curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' --retry 15 --retry-connrefused --retry-delay 2 "http://localhost:$PORT/"; kill "$(cat .agent-audit/env/boot.pid)"
     ```
     PowerShell: `Remove-Item Env:AUTH_SECRET` in place of `env -u`, the
     `Start-Process … -PassThru` recipe from 0.7 with `Wait-Process -Timeout 25`.
     Write the two log paths and exit codes to `boot.md`. An `instrumentation.ts`
     hook that is wired wrong is caught here: exit 124 with no error line
     means the gate did not fire, and the batch is not FIXED until it does.
  2. **Module proof** (only when 0.7 logged a start failure that is not an
     env var): `env -u AUTH_SECRET <ts> -e "import('./src/env.ts')"` → the
     named error pasted; the FIXED line carries `boot: BLOCKED-NO-RUNTIME
     (<notes.md line>)` and the manual boot check from rung 1.
  3. The env-module test passes (always, in addition to 1 or 2).
  4. `<run> build` still passes; `<run> typecheck` still passes.

**C. Fallbacks and divergence** (AGENT-SAFE; needs no deployed
knowledge)
- Classify every string fallback from check 2:

  | Class | Looks like | Disposition |
  |---|---|---|
  | safe default | `PORT ?? '3000'`, `LOG_LEVEL ?? 'info'`, a feature flag defaulting to off, a timeout, a page size | kept; listed as `safe default` with the line |
  | wrong-in-prod | a local host, `host.docker.internal`, a test / dev / placeholder value, a personal username or e-mail, a staging host, a sandbox API base URL, a dev key prefix (`sk_test_`, `pk_test_`) | C1 |
  | insecure default | `?? 'dev-secret'` for a signing key, `?? false` for TLS verification, a default-allow flag (`SKIP_AUTH`, `DISABLE_RLS`) | C3 |
  | correct in prod, wrong in preview / dev | an e-mail or callback link hard-wired to the production domain | C2 |

- **C1 (wrong-in-prod)** becomes "required in production": keep the dev
  default; throw a named error when `VERCEL_ENV === 'production'` (or
  `NODE_ENV === 'production'` off Vercel) and the var is unset. Helper in
  the env module: `prodRequired(name, devDefault)`. The behavior in
  production changes from "silently wrong" to "fails with a named error",
  which is the fix; it needs no knowledge of what production sets — if
  production sets the var, nothing changes; if it does not, production was
  already running against the wrong host. No `vercel env ls` output is
  required for this batch, so a missing CLI gates nothing here.
- **C2 (correct in prod, wrong elsewhere):** derive from the platform var
  (`VERCEL_ENV === 'preview' ? VERCEL_BRANCH_URL : VERCEL_PROJECT_PRODUCTION_URL`,
  with `https://` added) or make it explicit per environment in
  `.env.example`.
- **C3 (insecure default):** the var must be set explicitly in production:
  unset in production → throw (named error). The value it takes when set,
  and any change to what the code does when the bypass is on, is GATED-4
  and a handoff line to security-agent (row 4 / 5) in the same run.
- `VERCEL_URL` in user-facing links, e-mails, OAuth callbacks or redirects
  → the explicit app URL var (`APP_URL` / `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL`, added to
  `.env.example`) with the C2 derivation as its production fallback.
- A `NODE_ENV` branch with no production arm (check 3) gets one, and the
  production arm reads the var (C1 shape).
- Evidence (Track A): `env.test.ts` cases `production + unset → named
  error`, `development + unset → default`, pasted; plus the boot proof
  (rung 1) when the var is `boot` in `required.md`; check 2 re-run count
  before → after.
- Scope-ratio line in the report: `Fallbacks found N: safe-default N |
  fixed N | gated N | blocked N | handed off N` — the five sum to N.

**D. Client exposure** (AGENT-SAFE)
- A server-only var read in client code (check 5) → move the read to a
  server component, route handler or server action and pass down only the
  derived non-secret value (a boolean "configured", a public URL).
- Modules that read server secrets get `import 'server-only'` as the
  first line when the package is installed (0.2 "is installed" cell) and
  the framework is Next.js. When it is not installed: write the handoff
  line to deps-agent, and apply the no-package guard meanwhile — a local
  `src/lib/server-only.ts` containing `if (typeof window !== 'undefined')
  throw new Error('<module> is server-only and was imported into client
  code');` imported by the secret-reading module. It is runtime, not
  build-time; the FIXED line says `interim guard; package handoff
  written`, and the evidence is `node -e "globalThis.window={};
  import('./src/lib/server-only.ts')"` (via `<ts>`) → the named error.
  Scripts (`node --import tsx scripts/x.ts`) that import a guarded module
  crash under the real `server-only` package: split the env module into a
  core file with the schema (imported by scripts) and a Next-facing file
  that adds the guard and re-exports it. Verify by running one script
  after the change and pasting its first output line.
- A secret-named var with a public prefix (check 4) is CRITICAL: remove
  the client read and the public-prefixed name from code now, reading the
  same value under a non-public name server-side; the hosting-side rename
  and the rotation are GATED-1 / GATED-2 plus the security-agent handoff.
- `next.config.* env:` keys holding secrets → removed from `env:`; the
  server reads them from the env module; a public one becomes
  `NEXT_PUBLIC_`.
- Evidence (Track A): check 5 counts before → after; check 6 bundle grep
  by name, prefix and value-prefix → 0 hits after a rebuild (the three
  lines pasted); `<run> build` passes (with the real `server-only` package
  a client import now fails the build — paste the failing build line when
  you provoke it with a throwaway import, then remove the import).

**E. Logs, errors and responses** (AGENT-SAFE)
- Remove env values from log and error strings; log the var name and
  `set` / `unset` (or the value's length) instead. A health route that
  echoes config returns `{ configured: boolean }` per feature, never the
  value or the host.
- A `JSON.stringify(process.env)` / `console.log(env)` is deleted or
  replaced by a `redactEnv()` helper that prints names only.
- Evidence (Track A): every check 7 line → 0 after the batch (the seven
  commands pasted).

**F. Hygiene within row 12** (AGENT-SAFE)
- CRLF / whitespace (check 9): the schema's whitespace rule from B; the
  committed example files re-saved LF; `.gitattributes` gets `*.env*
  text eol=lf` when the repo has a `.gitattributes` or Windows developers
  (the CRLF hit itself is the evidence of the latter).
- Alias chains (check 11): consolidate to one name in code when the second
  name is `UNSET` in every deployed column of `required.md`; when a
  deployed environment sets the second name, GATED-2 (the rename steps).
- Secrets as CLI arguments in repo scripts (check 8): the script reads the
  value from `process.env` / the env module; the `package.json` script
  line stops passing it.
- Scripts without a loader (check 15): the loader import added as the
  first line, or the `--env-file` flag on the script line.
- Evidence (Track A): each check's count → 0, pasted.

**Routing of what you found but do not fix:** every security-agent,
deps-agent, audit-agent, docs-agent, test-agent and debug-agent lead from
Phase 2 is one line in `.agent-audit/handoffs/<owner>.md` in the universal
format, counted per owner in `## Handoffs`.

### HUMAN-GATE, exactly four things
Each is written up as the exact edit or command and never applied.
1. **Hosting and CI configuration values.** Any `vercel env add|rm|update`,
   dashboard edit, Vercel project policy or Node setting, CI secret or
   variable, Supabase key change (including the legacy → publishable /
   secret key switch), `fly secrets set`, `netlify env:set`, and the
   redeploy those need. Written up as: command — e.g. `vercel env add
   APP_URL production --visibility config`, one per environment, in
   `.agent-audit/env/staged/hosting-commands.md`.
2. **Renaming or removing a var that a deployed environment sets, or that
   another app sends or shares** (shared ingest secrets, tokens another
   service holds, an alias name a deployed environment sets). Written up
   as: diff — the code change — plus the per-environment and per-consumer
   command list from gate 1, in `.agent-audit/env/staged/rename-<VAR>.md`.
3. **Build-time (every-environment) validation** — importing the env
   module from `next.config.*`, or a CI step that fails the build on a
   missing var — when any required var's Prod / Preview / CI cell in
   `required.md` is `UNSET` or `BLOCKED-NO-NETWORK` (it would turn a
   preview or CI build red). Written up as: diff — the `next.config.*`
   import or the workflow step, in `.agent-audit/env/staged/build-time-validation.diff`.
4. **The deny-side semantics of an insecure-default flag** — what the code
   does when `SKIP_AUTH`, `DISABLE_RLS`, `WEBHOOK_SKIP_VERIFY` or a flag of
   that shape is set, and the default it takes outside production. The
   production "must be set explicitly" throw is applied (playbook C3);
   the rest is written up as: diff — in `.agent-audit/env/staged/flag-<VAR>.diff`,
   with the security-agent handoff line referenced.

### Standards (cited)
1. Config is strictly separated from code; the litmus test is whether the repo could be published without exposing a credential; vars are independent per deploy, not grouped into named environments.
   — The Twelve-Factor App, III. Config (12factor.net/config)
2. `NEXT_PUBLIC_` values are inlined into the browser bundle at `next build` and frozen; dynamic lookups (`process.env[name]`, destructured `process.env`) are not inlined.
   — Next.js Environment Variables guide (docs v16.3.8, updated 2026-08-25)
3. Load order is `process.env` → `.env.$(NODE_ENV).local` → `.env.local` (skipped when `NODE_ENV=test`) → `.env.$(NODE_ENV)` → `.env`; allowed `NODE_ENV` values are `production`, `development`, `test`; `.env*.local` is gitignored, `.env.test` may be committed; scripts outside Next use `@next/env` `loadEnvConfig`.
   — Next.js Environment Variables guide (v16.3.8, 2026-08-25)
4. Only the data access layer reads `process.env`; secret-holding modules import `server-only` so a client import fails the build.
   — Next.js Data Security guide (v16.3.8, 2026-08-25)
5. `instrumentation.ts` `register()` runs once per new server instance and must finish before requests are served; branch on `NEXT_RUNTIME`.
   — Next.js Instrumentation guide (v16.3.8, 2026-08-25)
6. t3-env: separate `server` / `client` schemas, strict `runtimeEnv`, `emptyStringAsUndefined`, any Standard Schema validator (zod included); importing the env file in `next.config` validates at build.
   — env.t3.gg/docs/nextjs (fetched 2026-10-02)
7. Vercel env changes apply only to new deployments; 64 KB total per deployment; Edge runtime functions and middleware are capped at 5 KB per variable; scopes are Production, Preview (optionally per branch), Development and custom environments.
   — Vercel Environment variables docs (updated 2026-09-17)
8. Vercel variables are typed Config or Secret: Secret values can't be viewed after saving; old "Sensitive" vars became Secrets; the "Separate Production Secret Values" policy requires production secrets to differ from other environments.
   — Vercel changelog, 2026-08-24
9. `VERCEL_URL` is the generated deployment host without `https://` and does not work with Standard Deployment Protection; `VERCEL_PROJECT_PRODUCTION_URL` is always set (also in previews) to the shortest production domain; `VERCEL_BRANCH_URL` is the branch alias host; `VERCEL_ENV` is production / preview / development.
   — Vercel System environment variables docs (updated 2026-07-15)
10. Supabase: publishable keys (`sb_publishable_`) are browser-safe; secret keys (`sb_secret_`) bypass RLS and return 401 when sent with a browser User-Agent; legacy `anon` / `service_role` keys are deprecated by the end of 2026.
    — Supabase API keys docs (fetched 2026-10-02)
11. CI: never store structured data (JSON/YAML) as one secret, since masking fails; register derived or re-encoded secrets with `::add-mask::`; secrets are not passed to fork-triggered workflows; avoid passing secrets on the command line; 48 KB per secret.
    — GitHub Docs, Using secrets in GitHub Actions; Security hardening for GitHub Actions (fetched 2026-10-02)
12. dotenv never overrides a var already set in the environment unless `override: true`; `.env` files are not committed.
    — motdotla/dotenv README FAQ (fetched 2026-10-02)
13. Node.js `--env-file=<path>` loads a dotenv-format file into `process.env` before the script runs (added v20.6.0; `--env-file-if-exists` added v22.9.0); assigning to `process.env` coerces the value to a string.
    — Node.js CLI and `process` docs (stable statements; this agent has no WebFetch, recorded 2026-10-10 from the base-fetch set, re-verified by docs-agent on a Node major bump)
14. Vite exposes to client code only variables prefixed with `VITE_` (or the `envPrefix` list) via `import.meta.env`; `.env.local` and `.env.[mode].local` are git-ignored by the template; `import.meta.env.*` values are statically replaced at build.
    — Vite docs, Env Variables and Modes (stable statements; recorded 2026-10-10, same caveat as 13)
15. pydantic-settings `BaseSettings` reads fields from the environment (case-insensitive by default) and from `env_file`; a field without a default is required and raises `ValidationError` naming the field at instantiation; `SecretStr` hides the value in `repr` and `str`.
    — pydantic-settings docs, Settings management (stable statements; recorded 2026-10-10, same caveat as 13)
16. `gh secret list` and `gh variable list` print names, scopes and update dates; secret values are never readable through the API or CLI.
    — GitHub CLI manual, `gh secret list` (stable statements; recorded 2026-10-10, same caveat as 13)

### Stack notes
Detect each feature from file or dependency evidence before applying its
rule, and record the evidence in `notes.md`. Project-specific var groups
(which three vars form one feature, which `AZURE_*` names an OAuth
provider's dashboard holds instead of the app) belong in your memory
notes for that repo, not here.
- **Next.js** (`next` in `package.json`).
  - Server-only vars read in a file under a `'use client'` boundary are
    `undefined` in the browser; find them with check 5.
  - `next.config.*` `env:` inlines values into the bundle like
    `NEXT_PUBLIC_`; any secret there is CRITICAL (check 5, playbook D).
  - Middleware / proxy runs in the Edge runtime on Next ≤15 unless
    configured otherwise: the 5 KB per-var Edge cap (Standard 7) applies to
    vars it reads; the env module imported there must read only the vars
    the edge path needs (a full server schema in middleware fails on
    missing server-only vars at the edge).
  - `server-only` throws when imported outside the `react-server`
    condition (playbook D script caveat).
  - `next build` runs the env module when `next.config.*` imports it
    (GATED-3); `instrumentation.ts` runs it at server start (AGENT-SAFE).
- **Vite / SPA** (`vite.config.*`): `VITE_` prefix rule (check 18);
  server code in the same repo (an Express API) reads `process.env`, the
  client reads `import.meta.env` — two inventories, one example file with
  both sections.
- **Expo** (`app.json` / `app.config.*`): `EXPO_PUBLIC_` only; secrets for
  EAS builds live in EAS, not the repo; `eas env:list` is read-only when
  the CLI is authenticated.
- **Vercel** (`vercel.json`, `.vercel/`).
  - Cron routes: `CRON_SECRET` is sent by Vercel Cron as `Authorization:
    Bearer <value>`; the var belongs in `.env.example` and in Production;
    the route's fail-closed behavior when it is unset is security-agent's
    (handoff when missing).
  - AI Gateway: on Vercel, auth comes from OIDC (`VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN`);
    `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` is for local development, so it is not required
    in the schema and its absence in production is `N/A — platform OIDC
    (Standard: Vercel AI Gateway docs)` in `required.md`, not a finding.
  - Secret-type vars for every server secret; Config-type only for values
    that are public anyway (check 13; GATED-1 to change types).
  - `vercel env ls` lists one entry per value: an entry scoped to two
    environments is one shared value (check 13).
- **Supabase** (`@supabase/supabase-js`, `@supabase/ssr`).
  - `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` and the anon / publishable key are public by
    design; the service-role / secret key never carries a public prefix
    and is read only in server-only modules (check 16, playbook D).
  - Legacy `anon` / `service_role` keys: HIGH with the switch steps
    (GATED-1): create publishable + secret keys, set both in every
    environment, deploy, then disable the legacy keys.
  - Edge functions read `Deno.env.get()` (1.1) and their secrets live in
    `supabase secrets list` (0.6).
- **Drizzle** (`drizzle.config.*`, `drizzle-kit`): drizzle-kit does not
  load Next's `.env.local` by itself; the config loads env explicitly
  (`@next/env` `loadEnvConfig` or `dotenv`). `DATABASE_URL` for migrations
  is the direct connection, not the pooler, when the docs in the repo say
  so; never print it.
- **Prisma** (`prisma/schema.prisma`): `env("DATABASE_URL")` in the schema
  is an env read — add `rg -o 'env\("([A-Z0-9_]+)"\)' -r '$1' prisma/*.prisma`
  to 1.1 when the file exists.
- **Docker / compose** (`Dockerfile*`, `compose.y*ml`): `ENV` bakes the
  value into the image (a secret there → security-agent); `ARG` secrets
  stay in layer history (→ audit-agent); `env_file:` and `environment:`
  are declarations (1.1); a compose service whose `environment:` names a
  var absent from `.env.example` is read-but-undeclared.
- **Fly / Netlify / Render**: `fly.toml [env]` and `netlify.toml
  [build.environment]` are declarations and are public in the repo — a
  secret there is a committed secret (security-agent); runtime secrets
  come from `fly secrets list` / `netlify env:list` (0.6).
- **Python** (`pyproject.toml`, `requirements*.txt`): `os.environ[...]`
  raises a bare `KeyError`; pydantic-settings recipe in playbook B;
  `python-dotenv` `load_dotenv()` is the loader scripts need (check 15
  equivalent: `rg -L 'load_dotenv' $(rg -l 'os\.environ' scripts)`).
- **GitHub Actions** (`.github/workflows/*`): every `secrets.X` used is in
  `workflow-refs.txt` and compared with `ci.txt` (a referenced secret that
  `gh secret list` does not show is a CI fresh-run breaker, CRITICAL);
  secret handling inside the workflow (echo, CLI args, job-level `env:`,
  `pull_request_target`) is audit-agent's (check 8 handoffs).
- **Windows dev machines:** env files saved with CRLF give values a
  trailing `\r` in some loaders (check 9); `$env:X` (PowerShell) vs
  `export X` (Git Bash) in docs; `env -u` exists in Git Bash, use
  `Remove-Item Env:X` in PowerShell; the boot proof has a PowerShell
  variant (0.7, playbook B).

### Static patterns
Every `rg` runs with the 1.1 glob set (`-g '!node_modules' -g '!.next'
-g '!dist' -g '!build' -g '!out' -g '!*.md' -g '!.git'`) and a path; the
expected-hit column is what a repo with no finding prints.

| Purpose | Pattern | Expected | A hit means |
|---|---|---|---|
| Env read, dot form | `rg -o 'process\.env\.([A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*)' -r '$1' .` | the inventory | one line in `read-dot.txt` |
| Env read, bracket / Vite / Python / Deno | `rg -o "process\.env\[['\"]([A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*)['\"]\]" -r '$1' .` / `rg -o 'import\.meta\.env\.([A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*)' -r '$1' .` / `rg -o "os\.(environ\[\|environ\.get\(\|getenv\()['\"]([A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*)" -r '$2' .` / `rg -o "Deno\.env\.get\(['\"]([A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*)" -r '$1' .` | the inventory | same |
| Dynamic read | `rg -n "process\.env\[[^'\"]\|=\s*process\.env\s*;\|\{[^}]*\}\s*=\s*process\.env\|process\.env\[\s*\`" .` | 0 | an inventory-incomplete point (`dynamic.txt`), and `undefined` in the browser for public names |
| Workflow secret / var reference | `rg -o '\$\{\{\s*(secrets\|vars)\.([A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*)' -r '$2' .github` | the CI inventory | compared with `ci.txt` |
| Dockerfile / compose declaration | `rg -o -P '^(ENV\|ARG)\s+([A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*)' -r '$2' Dockerfile*` | the Docker inventory | a declaration; a literal secret value → security-agent |
| Non-null assert | `rg -n -P 'process\.env\.[A-Z0-9_]+!' .` | 0 | unvalidated required read (check 1) |
| `as string` cast | `rg -n -P 'process\.env\.[A-Z0-9_]+\s+as\s+string' .` | 0 | same |
| Numeric coercion without guard | `rg -n -P '(parseInt\|Number\|parseFloat)\(\s*process\.env\.[A-Z0-9_]+' .` | 0 outside the env module | NaN at runtime (check 1) |
| String fallback | `rg -n -P "process\.env\.[A-Z0-9_]+\s*(\?\?\|\|\|)\s*['\"\`][^'\"\`]*['\"\`]" .` | only safe defaults, each listed | playbook C classification |
| Local-host fallback | `rg -n -P "(\?\?\|\|\|)\s*['\"\`](https?://)?(localhost\|127\.0\.0\.1\|0\.0\.0\.0\|host\.docker\.internal)" .` | 0 | wrong-in-prod (C1) |
| Test-value fallback | `rg -n -P "(\?\?\|\|\|)\s*['\"\`](test\|dev\|development\|secret\|changeme\|password\|admin\|xxx\|todo\|placeholder\|dummy)['\"\`]" .` | 0 | wrong-in-prod or insecure (C1 / C3) |
| Secret-looking literal fallback | `rg -n -P "(\?\?\|\|\|)\s*['\"](sk_\|pk_\|sb_secret_\|whsec_\|ghp_\|xox[bp]-\|AKIA\|postgres(ql)?://[^'\"]*:[^'\"]*@\|eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,})" .` | 0 | security-agent handoff + C1 |
| Default-allow flag | `rg -n -P "process\.env\.(SKIP\|DISABLE\|BYPASS\|ALLOW\|NO)_[A-Z0-9_]+\s*(\?\?\|\|\|)\s*['\"](true\|1)['\"]" .` | 0 | C3 + security-agent handoff |
| Alias chain | `rg -n -P 'process\.env\.([A-Z0-9_]+)\s*(\|\|\|\?\?)\s*process\.env\.([A-Z0-9_]+)' .` | 0 | two names for one value (check 11) |
| `NODE_ENV` comparison | `rg -n -P "(NODE_ENV\|VERCEL_ENV\|APP_ENV)\s*(===?\|!==?)\s*['\"]\w+['\"]" .` | each listed with its arms | check 3 |
| Secret-named public var | `rg -n -P '\b(NEXT_PUBLIC\|VITE\|REACT_APP\|PUBLIC\|EXPO_PUBLIC\|NUXT_PUBLIC)_[A-Z0-9_]*(SECRET\|SERVICE_ROLE\|PRIVATE\|PASSWORD\|TOKEN\|API_KEY\|SIGNING\|WEBHOOK)' .` | 0 | CRITICAL (check 4) |
| Server var in client file | `for f in $(rg -l "^['\"]use client['\"]" .); do rg -n -P 'process\.env\.(?!NEXT_PUBLIC_\|NODE_ENV)[A-Z]' "$f"; done` | 0 | `undefined` in the browser; playbook D |
| Config consumer in client file | `for f in $(rg -l "^['\"]use client['\"]" .); do rg -n '\b(env\|config\|settings)\.\w+' "$f"; done` | 0 for server exports | playbook D via the config module |
| `next.config` `env:` keys | `rg -n -A20 -P '^\s*env:\s*\{' next.config.*` | 0 secret-named keys | CRITICAL |
| Bundle leak by name / prefix | `rg -l -g '!*.map' '<server names>' .next/static dist build out` / `rg -l -g '!*.map' 'sb_secret_\|service_role\|sk_live_\|sk_test_\|whsec_\|-----BEGIN\|ghp_\|xox[bp]-\|AKIA\|postgres(ql)?://' .next/static dist build out` | 0 files | CRITICAL; playbook D, then security-agent for exploitability |
| Env in log call | `rg -n -P '\b(console\|logger\|log\|pino\|winston\|bunyan\|Sentry)\.[a-zA-Z]+\([^)]*process\.env' .` | 0 | playbook E |

| Secret as CLI argument (repo) | `rg -n -P '--(password\|passwd\|pwd\|token\|secret\|api-?key\|apikey\|auth)[= ]' scripts bin tools package.json Makefile Dockerfile* docker-compose*.y*ml` | 0 | playbook F |

### Per-finding format
```
[ID] <VAR or path:line> — <title>
  Class: Inventory | Validation | Fallback | Divergence | Client exposure | Logs | Hygiene | Parity | Secret (handoff)
  Severity: CRITICAL|HIGH|MEDIUM|LOW   Confidence: H|M|L
  Runtime: server | edge | client | script | cron | ci   Required?: boot | request | script | ci | inert-group:<name> | platform
  Standard / rule: <Standard N | playbook C class | check N>
  Where: <path:line, every occurrence>
  Disposition: FIXED | APPLIED-UNVERIFIED | STAGED | GATED-n | HANDOFF-<owner> | BLOCKED-<code> | ACCEPTED-RISK | REVERTED
  In production, with this var unset, the app will: <one sentence>   (Fallback and Divergence classes)
  Fix: <what changed, before → after, or the staged file path>
  Evidence: <comm count / boot log path + exit code / test name + pass count / bundle grep lines / check N count before → after>
```
Severity: CRITICAL = a secret-named var with a public prefix, a server
secret in the bundle, a required var `UNSET` in Production, a referenced
CI secret that does not exist; HIGH = an unvalidated `boot` var, a
wrong-in-prod fallback, an insecure default, a legacy Supabase key, a
tracked env file; MEDIUM = read-but-undeclared, env value in a log,
`VERCEL_URL` in a user-facing link, alias chains; LOW = declared-but-
unread, CRLF, doc drift, a non-inlinable public read in dead code.
